title: Australian Stock Assessment Community of Practice 2026
text:
We are very excited to welcome you to our first annual Australian Stock Assessment Community of Practice Workshop!
Our Community of Practice was officially launched in April 2026, with the mission to build a collaborative community of stock assessment practitioners to better support sustainable fisheries management. You can read more about us in our 1-page summary (link here).



Time: 10-14 August, 9am–5pm AEST
Location: Ecosciences Precinct (Conference Room, Ground Floor), 41 Boggo Rd, Dutton Park QLD—or online
Cost: Free. Travel and meals are at the expense of attendees.

Register your interest in the event here!

title: Welcome to our first annual Australian Stock Assessment Community of Practice Workshop!
text:
Who is this conference for?
This workshop will comprise of two parts:

Days 1 to 2 of this workshop is generally aimed at stock assessment scientists. The schedule contains conference style activities for introduction and networking.
Days 3 to 5 is aimed at both stock assessment scientists and fishery managers. Over these three days, Prof Andre Punt will lead his course “MSE with Managers”.

If you are unsure which part is best for you, get in touch.
There is limited capacity in the room so we will prioritise stock assessment science practitioners for in person attendance.
All 5 days of the workshop will be delivered in a hybrid format (both online and in person).

title: Additional information
text:
The Ecosciences Precinct (41 Boggo Rd, Dutton Park QLD) is a short, 200-meter walk from Boggo Road/Park Road train station.




All public transport fares in Queensland cost 50 cents. Contactless payment is available on all South East Queensland (SEQ) trains, trams, ferries and buses—you can use your digital or physical bank card to tap on and off.
The workshop will be held in the conference room on the ground floor, before the security check point.
On-site parking could be arranged. Get in touch with us for options.

text:
Food and drink

Lunch
There is a cafe on-site (Hey Mr Dutton Park) with several excellent food options. If you would like to eat there, please consider pre-ordering your food upon arrival each morning so we don’t overwhelm the staff at lunch time. There are additional cafes within a 10-minute walking radius.


Dinner
Group dinners will be organised for each night from Monday to Thursday. These dinners are optional and will be pay-your-own-way. We will book restaurants within a 20-minute walking radius from the workshop and confirm numbers each morning.
If you have any dietary requirements that you would like to be considered when booking dinner locations, please contact us by 1 August.


Morning and afternoon tea
Tea and coffee will be provided on site.


Accommodation
There are ample accommodation options, either walking distance or accessible via public transport.

Bring your laptop (required for hands-on sessions)

Bring a notebook or pen for quick notes

If you are attending Days 1–2

Prepare for the lightning round
Work with your jurisdiction to create a poster
Consider volunteering to lead parts of the workshop. If you are interested, get in touch!



If you are attending Days 3–5

Install required software (details to be provided)

Ensure your laptop is fully updated

Confirm you can install and run R / required tools



🎤 Lightning round
Prepare a short introduction (~2 minutes):

your name

your organisation

one current challenge

one thing you hope to learn



🖼️ Poster session
As a jurisdiction, bring a poster representing your work, team, or context. This is intentionally flexible! Ideas include:

a flagship stock assessment

a challenging case study

your team and region (“getting to know us”)

a methodological innovation

a collaboration success story



🙋‍♀️ Volunteer to contribute
We are looking for volunteers to help lead parts of the workshop. If you are interested, get in touch!
Opportunities include:

Session chairs and general facilitators
Delivering Lecture 3: What is MSE? (~45 min) on Monday
Leading a Curated Narrative Session on Tuesday

Curated narrative sessions will consist of a 20–25 min presentation with ~20 min discussion
Possible themes:

Navigating data-limited situations
→ How you selected and applied an approach
Working across jurisdictions on shared stocks
→ Coordination challenges and solutions
When standard approaches don’t fit
→ Adapting methods to unusual situations
Building stakeholder trust through assessment
→ Communication and transparency
From problem to solution: a challenging assessment journey
→ Lessons learned from a difficult case

Better yet, post them in either our LinkedIn forum (for Network members) or GitHub discussion board (for formal members).
